request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export tree people (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-tree"`), and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`, including the main tree-export test.

**What the file contains:** the header `sheet,name,grade,due-total`, then one line per person. The current sheet's people come first in list order, then each other sheet in the tree, sorted by sheet id. The whole tree means the topmost ancestor and everything below it, so it also covers sibling sheets, not just the current sheet's parents and children. The grade is the one in force on that sheet's today. The due-total is the same value the person's row shows, `n/a` included.

**How it's built:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/whole-tree`, defined in `rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/whole-tree.GET.yml` and handled by `RespondWithWholeTree.java`. It returns every sheet id in the tree using the existing `SettingStore.wholeTree`. Nothing in the stored data changed.
- **Front end:** `features/people/tree-export.slot.tsx`, modelled on the existing tree search. When pressed, it fetches the tree list and re-reads the other sheets from the store. It then builds the lines one sheet at a time and downloads the file.

**Two choices the request didn't settle:**
- Retired people are included, as the existing people and claims exports do.
- The export always shows the tree as it is now and ignores any as-of date on screen, the same as the tree search.

The tests check only a parent and one child sheet, so sibling sheets and the ordering of more than two sheets are untested.
